subject: Emergency regional reroute guidance — immediate action recommended
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@globex.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-01T08:12:00Z
Subject: Production errors — EU requests failing (500s)

Markus,

We started seeing 500 errors for all requests routed to eu-1 this morning (08:05 UTC). Error rate is ~45% for our ingestion endpoint and it’s impacting our nightly batch. Can you confirm if this is a known incident and what the mitigation steps are? Our engineers are standing by.

Log sample: 500 InternalServerError — token routing failed (kv cache miss).

CC: acme-eng@globex.com

Thanks,
Emma Jones
Senior Platform Engineer
Globex Corporation

---

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@globex.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-01T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Production errors — EU requests failing (500s)

Emma —

Thanks for the alert and the log sample. We’re actively investigating a partially degraded control plane in eu-1 that is triggering a higher-than-normal error rate for new connections. Engineering has provisioned a temporary routing policy to bypass the eu-1 control plane and route compatible sessions to eu-2 and us-west while we remediate.

Immediate actions for Globex (recommended, low-risk):
1) If you call our API with a region override header, set X-Redwood-Region: eu-2 or X-Redwood-Region: us-west. This will route new sessions away from eu-1.
2) For long-running sessions, you can set the prefer_local_kv=false parameter to avoid KV-cache lookups tied to eu-1 (reduces latency slightly but avoids errors).
3) We’ve attached a short playbook (reroute_playbook_v2.pdf) with curl examples and sample SDK flags for Node/Python.

We’ll keep this thread updated. I’ve cc’d Lauren and Marissa for escalation and account coordination. If you want us to flip routing at the account level (server-side override) we can do that; tell us when you’re ready and we’ll apply a temporary account policy that forces region routing for all your tokens.

Status link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2028-07-01

Markus Klein
Support Lead, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0172

Attachment: reroute_playbook_v2.pdf (7 pages) — quick steps and rollback notes

- Lauren

—acme-eng on behalf of Globex platform team

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@globex.com>, markus_klein@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-02T15:40:00Z
Subject: Incident closure & follow-up actions — 2028-07-01 eu-1 partial control plane failure

Hi Emma / Globex team —

Thanks again for the rapid response and cooperation. Final update and postmortem summary below.

What happened:
- On 2028-07-01 07:58 UTC a configuration propagation bug caused a subset of control-plane requests in eu-1 to fail during session setup, increasing error rate for new sessions.

What we did to mitigate:
- 08:10 UTC: Temporary routing policy applied to route new sessions from eu-1 -> eu-2 and us-west for compatibility.
- 08:22 UTC: Customer communication with SDK/header examples; reroute_playbook_v2.pdf attached.
- 08:30 UTC: Account-level override enabled for Globex at their request.
- 11:15 UTC: Root cause identified and control-plane process restarted; soft recovery observed.
- 12:00 UTC: Full configuration reconciliation completed; eu-1 normalized.

Customer impact and timeline:
- Globex saw error spikes between ~08:05–08:30 UTC; switching to eu-2 reduced errors to <1% for new sessions.

Follow-up actions (next 30 days):
1) Deploy a guardrail to prevent stale propagation state from being served (SRE ticket SRE-2879).
2) Add an automated account-level fallback toggle for critical customers (Product/Platform).
3) Update runbooks and add the attached incident_log_20280701.csv to the internal incident binder.
4) CS will coordinate a goodwill credit for impacted usage; Lauren will confirm amount.

If you’d like a scheduled postmortem call, we can set aside 30 minutes for the technical review — propose Tue 2028-07-05 16:00 UTC.

Apologies for the disruption. We’ll share the formal postmortem doc once internal review is complete.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability
Jonas_Weber@redwood.ai

Attachment: incident_log_20280701.csv (accounted events & timestamps)
